title: Are Large Language Model-based Evaluators the Solution to Scaling Up Multilingual Evaluation?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the class distribution of LLM-generated evaluation scores against human annotations across multiple metrics, revealing a systemic tendency for the LLM to disproportionately assign the highest possible scores (e.g., 2) even when human annotators disagree or provide lower scores.

Evaluating the Percentage Agreement (PA) between LLM evaluators and human annotators across 8 different languages, showing that evaluator reliability degrades and positivity bias is amplified in lower-resource languages (e.g., Czech) and non-Latin script languages (e.g., Chinese, Japanese) compared to high-resource Latin-script languages.
